def-singular-instanton-knot-and-sutured-.source_excerpt: Parallel transport (holonomy) around either meridian is conjugate in $SU(2)$ to $\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)$; its image has order two in $PU(2)$.
def-singular-instanton-knot-and-sutured-.proposed_replacement: As the radius of a meridional circle tends to zero, its holonomy conjugacy class tends to that of $\operatorname{diag}(i,-i)$ in $SU(2)$; the limiting image has order two in $PU(2)$. This is the prescribed asymptotic meridional holonomy, not an assertion of exact holonomy on every finite-radius circle for an arbitrary smooth $A_0$. For a flat connection the holonomies of homotopic meridional circles are conjugate, so their conjugacy class is exactly this limiting class.

cex-ip-infinite-dimensional-pointwise-de.source_excerpt: 1.2 Suppose that $\lambda$ is a translation-invariant Borel measure finite on every bounded Borel set. Put $U_j=\{x:\|x-e_j\|_2<1/3\}$. For $j\ne k$, $\|e_j-e_k\|_2=\sqrt2>2/3$, so the $U_j$ are pairwise disjoint. Each lies in the bounded ball $\{x:\|x\|_2<2\}$ by the triangle inequality. Translation invariance gives $\lambda(U_j)=m$ independent of $j$. If $m>0$, the first $N$ disjoint balls have total measure $Nm$ for every $N$, contradicting finiteness of the radius-two ball. Hence $m=0$. [F2, given, algebra]
cex-ip-infinite-dimensional-pointwise-de.proposed_replacement: 1.2 Suppose that $\lambda$ is a nonzero locally finite translation-invariant Borel measure, where locally finite means that every point has a neighborhood of finite measure. At zero choose $R>0$ with $\lambda(B(0,R))<\infty$. Put $r=R/8$ and $U_j=B((R/2)e_j,r)$. For $j\ne k$ the distance between the centers is $R/\sqrt2>2r$, so these balls are pairwise disjoint, and every $U_j$ lies in $B(0,R)$ because $R/2+r<R$. Translation invariance gives a common finite mass $m=\lambda(U_j)$. If $m>0$, finite additivity and monotonicity give $Nm\le\lambda(B(0,R))$ for every $N$, a contradiction. Hence $m=0$. This covers in particular every measure finite on all bounded Borel sets, since that condition implies local finiteness. [F2, F4, given, algebra]

cex-ip-infinite-dimensional-pointwise-de.source_excerpt: 2.1 Translation invariance and step 1.2 make every radius-$1/3$ ball have measure zero. Let $D$ be the set of finitely supported rational sequences. [F3] makes $D$ countable: it is the countable union, over support lengths $N$, of the countable set $\mathbb Q^N$ padded with zeros. It is dense in $\ell^2$: for any $x\in\ell^2$ and $\epsilon>0$, choose $N$ so that the squared tail sum is less than $\epsilon^2/4$, then approximate the first $N$ coordinates by rationals with squared total error less than $\epsilon^2/4$; the resulting padded vector is within $\epsilon$ of $x$. The radius-$1/3$ balls centered at $D$ therefore form a countable cover of $\ell^2$. By [F2], $\lambda(\ell^2)=0$, and [F4] makes every Borel subset null. This contradicts that $\lambda$ is nonzero. Hence no such reference measure exists, refuting the statement; in particular, the displayed Gaussian has no density relative to one. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.2, given, algebra, choose] ∎

ex-knot-kt-15-worked-cases.source_excerpt: The universal-cover rectangle below has horizontal coordinate $\mu$ and vertical coordinate $\lambda$; opposite sides are identified. The red segment ends at $(2,1)$, so it represents the image $2\mu+\lambda$ of the longitude. The picture illustrates the slope convention only; the verification computes the map directly.
ex-knot-kt-15-worked-cases.proposed_replacement: The displayed rectangle is a two-unit-square window in the universal cover $\mathbb R^2$ of the torus $\mathbb R^2/\mathbb Z^2$, with horizontal coordinate $\mu$ and vertical coordinate $\lambda$. The identifications are $(x,y)\sim(x+m,y+n)$ for all integers $m,n$, so each unit square is a fundamental domain. The red lifted segment ends at $(2,1)$ and therefore represents the image $2\mu+\lambda$ of the longitude. The picture illustrates the slope convention only; the verification computes the map directly.
